papers.title: Hybrid cultured meat as an integrated food production system: Recent advances and commercialization challenges.
papers.abstract: Hybrid cultured meat (HCM) has emerged as a promising strategy to improve the food applicability of cultured meat (CM) by combining cultured animal cells with animal-free derived materials. This review synthesizes recent advances in HCM research published between 2021 and 2026, and examines HCM as an integrated food production system rather than as a simple extension of conventional CM. The review focuses on cell sources, animal-free scaffolds, serum-free media (SFM), 3D bioprinting, bioprocess scale-up, sensory and nutritional properties, consumer acceptance, and regulatory considerations. Recent studies show that HCM can reduce the cultured biomass burden per unit of product while using animal-free materials to support structure, expand formulation options, and improve compatibility with food processing. Progress has been reported in co-culture strategies, edible scaffolds, food-grade SFM, structuring for texture and marbling, and nutritional customization. However, most current systems remain at laboratory or prototype scale, and several commercialization barriers remain, including scalable cell supply, cost-effective media, scaffolds, texturization, consumer acceptance, and regulatory clarity. We argue that HCM progress will depend less on isolated optimization of individual technologies and more on the integration of cell supply, scaffold design, media, scale-up, and product-quality targets into scalable food-production workflows. This systems view positions HCM as a near-term route toward more commercially realistic CM products.

papers.title: Topological transitions and graded wall thicknesses cooperatively boost mechanical and mass-transport behavior in TPMS Mg-scaffolds
papers.abstract: Hybrid scaffolds combining various Triply Periodic Minimal Surface architectures enable coordinated functional performance. However, their direct assembly introduces geometric discontinuities at the interfaces, leading to compromised mechanical and fluidic properties. Here, a gradient transition region is designed to facilitate smooth topological evolution between Primitive and Gyroid structures, while a wall-thickness gradient modulates stiffness and pore characteristics. The scaffolds are fabricated via laser powder bed fusion using WE43 alloy. Results demonstrate that the hybrid scaffold achieved an elastic modulus of 1.20 GPa and a yield strength of 43.64 MPa, marking increases of approximately 39% and 56% over a uniform‑wall‑thickness hybrid counterpart. The results reveal that the graded structural distribution effectively disperses external loads across adjacent unit cells and the transition zone, suppressing local instabilities and delaying early interfacial failure. Meanwhile, the permeability reaches 9.6 × 10 − ⁹ m², approaching that of the highly permeable Gyroid scaffold, since the continuously evolving pore morphology mitigates velocity fluctuations and pressure accumulation caused by localized channel constrictions. These attributes establish a synergistic optimization mechanism, in which the Primitive region provides structural support and load transfer, the Gyroid region facilitates efficient mass transport, and the graded transition zone ensures mechanical and fluidic compatibility between them. This strategy alleviates the stiffness-permeability trade-off within the investigated design space by integrating the complementary functions of the two topologies within a continuously graded architecture.

papers.title: Modular Biofabrication of Functional Skeletal Muscle Incorporated with Endothelialized Microvascular Seed‐Derived Lumenized Microvessels
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The clinical translation of engineered skeletal muscle (eSM) for volumetric muscle regeneration is hindered by the challenge of establishing a functional vascular network capable of sustaining its high metabolic demand and ensuring graft survival. Here, we present a bottom‐up biofabrication strategy to generate a pre‐vascularized in vitro eSM model through the modular assembly of independently matured muscle and vascular compartments. C2C12 myoblasts were encapsulated within core–shell fibers using rotary wet‐spinning (RoWS), yielding anisotropically aligned, multinucleated, and contractile myofibers expressing myosin heavy chain and sarcomeric α‐actinin. In parallel, gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA)‐based microvascular seeds (µVS), pre‐endothelialized with human umbilical vein endothelial cells, were engineered to guide rapid and structurally stable vascular formation while preventing uncontrolled capillary self‐organization. Fully endothelialized µVS were incorporated into a pro‐angiogenic bioink and processed via RoWS to generate tubular vascular fibers with physiological diameters (100–200 µm) and continuous CD31‐positive lumens. After independent maturation, muscle and vascular constructs were bioassembled into a hierarchically organized tissue and co‐cultured. By decoupling myogenic and angiogenic differentiation, this strategy overcomes medium incompatibility typical of conventional co‐cultures, preserving compartment‐specific architecture and function and establishing a versatile platform for muscle‐vascular modeling and translational muscle repair.

papers.title: Validation of the Italian version of the HOOS-12 in people with total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Abstract Background The Hip disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (HOOS) is a widely used patient-reported outcome measures for assessing symptoms, physical function, and health-related quality of life (QoL) in individuals with hip disorders. Although the full version has been validated across several languages, including Italian, its length may limit feasibility in time-constrained clinical settings. A 12-item short version (HOOS-12) was developed to improve feasibility while retaining core domains of pain, function, and QoL, showing good measurement properties. This study aimed to validate the Italian HOOS-12 and evaluate its measurement properties in patients with total hip arthroplasty. Methods Demographic and clinical data of adult patients with total hip arthroplasty hospitalized for acute inpatient rehabilitation were retrospectively obtained. Participants completed the full HOOS, the Harris Hip Score (HHS), and the Functional Independence Measure at both admission and discharge. HOOS-12 scores were derived from the corresponding items of the full HOOS. Structural validity was assessed using confirmatory factor analysis, and multi-group analysis was conducted to explore measurement invariance for cross-cultural validity. Construct validity and responsiveness were evaluated through a-priori hypothesis testing based on correlation analyses and effect sizes. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach’s alpha. Floor and ceiling effects were also examined. All analyses were conducted in accordance with COSMIN guidelines. Results Confirmatory factor analysis supported the three-factor structure (pain, function, and QoL) of the HOOS-12. Total and subscale scores generally showed strong correlations with the full HOOS and the HHS scores, confirming 77% of a-priori hypotheses. Responsiveness was supported by large effect sizes and moderate-to-strong correlations between change scores of the HOOS-12 and those of the comparator instruments. Changes in total HOOS-12 also discriminate between improved and not-improved patients based on changes in HHS. Internal consistency was generally good across domains. A ceiling effect was observed only in the pain domain at discharge. Conclusions The Italian version of the HOOS-12 demonstrated good structural validity, construct validity, internal consistency, and responsiveness in patients undergoing acute rehabilitation after total hip arthroplasty. Its brevity and adequate measurement performance support its use in clinical practice and research within Italian-speaking populations. Trial registration Not applicable.

papers.title: Posterior Maxillary Segmental Osteotomy–A Paradigm Shift From Orthognathic Surgery to Preprosthetic Surgery: A Case Report
papers.abstract: Severe supraeruption of maxillary molars following loss of opposing mandibular teeth can critically reduce interarch space and compromise implant-prosthetic rehabilitation. When extrusion is extensive, orthodontic intrusion or prosthetic reduction may be impractical. Posterior maxillary segmental osteotomy (PMSO), classically indicated in orthognathic surgery, can be repurposed as a pre-prosthetic intervention to restore vertical dimension and occlusal harmony. Two patients presenting with missing mandibular posterior teeth and marked supraeruption of opposing maxillary molars exhibited interarch space of <5 mm. After clinical and radiographic evaluation, PMSO was planned to reposition the extruded maxillary posterior segment. Osteotomy lines were executed under local anesthesia, and the segment was repositioned using a prefabricated surgical stent for guidance and stabilization. Simultaneous placement of endosseous implants was performed in the mandibular posterior region. Patients were followed radiographically and clinically to assess bony union, implant osseointegration, pulpal vitality, and segment stability. Both cases demonstrated satisfactory repositioning of the maxillary segment with immediate restoration of interarch space adequate for prosthetic rehabilitation. Follow-up imaging confirmed successful bony union and implant osseointegration. No postoperative complications, including segmental necrosis, relapse, or pulpal injury, were observed. Definitive prosthetic rehabilitation was completed after three months with stable occlusal relationships and improved function. papers.title: Solving elliptic partial differential equation based on deep reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: Elliptic partial differential equations (PDEs) constitute a fundamental class of governing equations in physics and engineering, underpinning the mathematical descriptions of electrostatic potential distribution, steady-state heat conduction, and linear elasticity. The numerical solution of these equations on fine discretization grids is computationally intensive, as classical iterative solvers require numerous sweeps to achieve convergence. This computational bottleneck critically hinders real-time applications such as online process control, interactive design optimization, and inverse problem reconstruction, where rapid response to changing boundary conditions or source terms is essential. The traditional numerical method cannot meet the real-time application requirements because of its long calculation time when solving on fine grids. In this study, the solution framework of deep Q-network is constructed, and the elliptic PDE solution is modeled as Markov decision processes. The state space includes solution field, residual field and boundary mark on discrete grid. The action space is 11 discrete corrections (− 0.10 to 0.10 with an interval of 0.02). The reward function is weighted sum of PDE residual term (weight 0.6), boundary error term (weight 0.3) and smooth regularization term (weight 0.1). The feature extraction network uses three-layer convolution and two residual blocks to output 512-dimensional vectors. The proposed DRL solver achieves relative L2 errors of 0.28%, 0.39%, and 0.62% on Poisson, Helmholtz, and anisotropic diffusion test cases, respectively, outperforming the finite element method (0.32%, 0.45%, 0.78%) and the multigrid method (0.31%, 0.44%, 0.76%). In the inference phase, the DRL solver completes a single forward pass on a 256 × 2562 grid in 0.15 s, achieving a 9898-fold speedup over the multigrid method’s 14.8 s. The training process converges stably within 20,000 steps, with the residual norm decreasing from an initial value of 12.4 to a final value of 0.16. This method provides a feasible way for solving and controlling real-time physical fields.

papers.title: Femoral Stem Design Influences Early Periprosthetic Fracture Risk Following Total Hip Arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Background Periprosthetic femur fracture (PFF) is a significant complication following total hip arthroplasty (THA). Modern collared, triple-taper metaphyseal-filling stems may reduce fracture risk. This study compared a triple-taper metaphyseal stem with other cementless designs to assess early PFF risk, fracture risk by age and bone quality, and the impact of collar position. Methods This retrospective study analyzed 774 primary cementless THAs, including triple-taper metaphyseal (n = 311), single-wedge (n = 294), double-wedge (n = 116), and gradual taper/metadiaphyseal-filling (n = 53) stems. Triple-taper stems were implanted through a prospective multicenter trial, while comparison stems were from a single health system. Patients were stratified by stem design, age, Dorr classification, and collar position. The primary outcome was 90-day PFF. Results PFF occurred in 53 patients (6.8%), including 15 (1.9%) postoperative fractures requiring reoperation. Patients with PFF were older ( P < .001) and predominantly female ( P = .02). Triple-taper stems demonstrated lower PFF risk than other designs (odds ratio 0.20; 95% confidence interval, 0.08–0.48; P < .001). PFF rates were 1.9% for triple-taper, 7.8% for single-wedge, 14.7% for double-wedge, and 13.2% for gradual taper stems (all P < .001). Differences persisted across age groups and Dorr A/B femurs. Proud collar positioning increased PFF risk (6.3% vs 0.8%; P = .02). Conclusions Collared, triple-taper metaphyseal stems were associated with lower early PFF risk across patient ages and bone quality profiles. Seating the collar on the calcar further reduced fracture incidence.

papers.title: A Multi‐Crosslinkable Methacrylated Alginate‐GelMa Bioink for Drop‐on‐Demand Bioprinting
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT To advance biofabrication, this work presents the development of a multi‐crosslinkable bioink based on methacrylated alginate di‐aldehyde (ADAMa) combined with gelatine methacryloyl (GelMa). ADAMa was synthesized using methacrylic anhydride under specific conditions, and successful functionalization as well as changes in chain length were confirmed by NMR (Nuclear Magnetic Resonance), ATR‐FTIR (Attenuated Total Reflectance—Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy), and GPC (Gel Permeation Chromatography) analyses. The resulting ADAMa–GelMa bioink can be crosslinked via several independent mechanisms, including UV‐initiated photopolymerization, enzymatic crosslinking, Schiff‐base formation, and ionic gelation with calcium ions. Our study confirms an increase in the compressive modulus with increasing GelMa content, ranging from 0.3 to 30 kPa, and in vitro biocompatibility for ADAMa–GelMa bioink with enhanced cell–material interaction for a 25:75 ADAMa–GelMa ratio. Furthermore, Drop‐on‐Demand (DoD) bioprinting performance was evaluated using filament fusion test and grid structure test analyses, along with structural fidelity assessment of free‐standing pillar arrays, including metrics such as pillar height and spacing. Multiphoton microscopy further revealed homogeneous cell distribution within printed pillars. Overall, this system provides tuneable mechanical properties, high cell viability, and strong structural fidelity, making it a promising candidate for the fabrication of complex, cell‐laden constructs in advanced biofabrication applications.

papers.title: Energy-based physics-informed neural networks with stochastic minibatching for phase-field modeling of fracture
papers.abstract: This work presents an efficient energy-based physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for phase-field modeling of fracture, in which the potential energy is estimated from stochastic minibatches of the integration points to reduce training cost. Building on the deep energy method (DEM), the network is trained by directly minimizing the regularized potential energy of the body rather than the residual of the governing equations. At each optimization step, the energy integral is evaluated on a randomly drawn subset of the integration points and rescaled so that the estimate is unbiased with respect to the full-grid quadrature energy. The framework is verified on a set of established fracture benchmarks, reproducing the expected crack development, including interacting and curved crack paths. Benchmarking reveals minibatching reduces the total training time by up to 50% relative to full-batch training, while preserving the crack trajectory. Furthermore, we extend the proposed model to hydrogen-assisted fracture, and it captures the coupled stress-hydrogen interaction where the drop in fracture toughness caused by hydrogen promotes earlier crack initiation and reduced load-carrying capacity. The results indicate that energy-based PINNs, combined with minibatch estimation of the discretized energy, offer an efficient route to phase-field fracture simulation and its multiphysics extensions.

papers.title: The emerging role of nanocellulose as a biomaterial in biomedical research: a bibliometric systematic analysis
papers.abstract: Nanocellulose (NC) has gained increasing attention as a sustainable and multifunctional biomaterial for biomedical applications. This work presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of NC research in biomedicine, integrating 3267 publications (2004–2024) retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and analyzed under a PRISMA-adapted protocol using VOSviewer. The workflow methodology comprised four stages: identification, screening, eligibility, and inclusion. Then, a rigorous data refinement through synonym unification and keyword harmonization was carried out. Both performance analysis and science mapping were conducted to quantify research output and visualize thematic structures, collaboration patterns, and citation networks. The temporal evolution revealed three distinct phases: an emerging phase (2004–2013) focused on fundamentals of NC production and biocompatibility; a consolidation phase (2014–2018) characterized by applications in scaffolds, wound healing, and drug-delivery; and an expansion phase (2019–2024) marked by diversification into 3D bioprinting, hybrid composites, and regenerative scaffolds. Three major research fronts were identified: i) regenerative scaffolds and bioprinting, dominated by NC–alginate and RGD-functionalized hydrogels; ii) nanomaterial development, emphasizing surface oxidation, carbodiimide coupling, and polymer hybridization; and iii) clinical applications, led by bacterial cellulose in antibacterial wound dressings and drug-release systems. The shift from materials-oriented studies toward translational research highlights both scientific maturity and remaining clinical gaps. Emerging trends such as sustainable BC production, stimuli-responsive hydrogels, and biosensing applications align with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals 3 and 12, positioning NC as a scalable and eco-efficient platform for next-generation biomedical technologies.

papers.title: Robust Local Stability and Bifurcation Control of Cubic-Intuitionistic-Fuzzy Fractional Jerk Dynamics with Nonlocal Physics-Informed Learning
papers.abstract: Fractional nonlinear systems combine the long memory dynamics and high parameter sensitivity. This brings difficulties for control design as well as accurate numerical approximation when unknown coefficients exist. In this paper, a computational method is proposed for a commensurate Caputo fractional jerk system with damping, stiffness, cubic-restoring, and fractional-order parameters modeled by cubic-intuitionistic-fuzzy (CIF) coefficient projections. Membership, nonmembership, and embedded point components are transmitted individually without defuzzification. We choose a full-state feedback law via an exhaustive restricted gain search at each vertex of the CIF outer support. The controller must have a Matignon angular margin of at least 25° and a worst eigenvalue real part no more than -0.25. For the chosen gain K = (1.1,0.6,0.8), the worst outer-support angular margin is 25.8757° with a maximum real part of -0.25210. The Matignon margin is expanded to 47.5089°, the pitchfork threshold is moved from μ = 0 to μ = k 1 = 1.1 outside the whole uncertain range 0.25 ≤ μ ≤ 0.65, and the origin is shifted from unstable to stable at the nominal position via feedback. Caputo trajectories are obtained by means of an Adams–Bashforth–Moulton predictor–correct–evaluate approach. Observed orders from a step-refinement research range from 1.94 to 2.24. The maximal terminal state norm is 0.04087 across 60 outer-support samples. The integrated state energy is reduced by 17.44 times with the nominal controller, and the control energy is 0.33934. A label-free fractional physics-informed neural network is trained using a dense L1 Caputo memory operator and precise initial-condition embedding too. It reproduces the dominating displacement with R 2 =0.9425, but lesser accuracy for the third small-amplitude condition reveals a present constraint of global physics-only training. The paradigm therefore unifies interpretable fractional stability, uncertainty propagation, resilient control, convergent temporal integration, and transparent physics-informed approximation for nonlinear systems with memory. In this research, robustness refers to the vertextested local fractional stability at the origin, rather than a theorem about global nonlinear stabilization or continuous-box sector stability.

papers.title: Beyond Exhaustive Simulation: Uncertainty-Aware Machine Learning for Power Delay Optimization in CMOS VLSI
papers.abstract: The simultaneous power and delay minimization has become an important challenge in VLSI due to deep nanometre scaling of CMOS technology. Due to the non-linear and combinatorial interaction of supply voltage, threshold-voltage assignment, transistor sizing, body biasing, and buffer insertion, exhaustive design space exploration based on SPICE is infeasible. This paper proposes a framework of alternating optimization aided by a Machine Learning Algorithm in which most of the simulator calls are replaced with a surrogate of a learnt model. Graph neural networks based on transformer capture netlist long-range dependencies, and physics-informed networks embed analytical power-delay relationships. Multi-objective Bayesian optimization looks in the surrogate using expected hypervolume improvement, and calibrated uncertainty from deep kernel learning is supplied for importance-weighted active learning. The framework has shown a mean power reduction of 31.2% and a mean delay reduction of 21.4% yielding a 45.8% power-delay product improvement on eight digital benchmarks. The implementation takes 25 times less wall-clock time compared to simulation-driven search. The reported error in surrogate for power is 1.9% and 1.7% for delay. Optimization of CMOS VLSI circuits is uncertainty-aware and data-efficient..

papers.title: Computational Validation of the Taylor Cellular Recoverability Scale: 600-Trial Digital Twin Simulation and PINN Trajectory Reconstruction
papers.abstract: This article presents a computational evaluation of the Taylor Cellular Recoverability Scale (CRS), a proposed multidimensional framework for characterizing cellular condition, pathological progression, and the capacity for recovery through dynamic system behavior. Using synthetic digital twin simulations, the study examines the framework’s four principal state variables: proximity to the Cellular Point of No Return (CPNR), drift velocity and trajectory, metabolic and energetic reserve, and homeostatic elasticity. Across a 600-system baseline cohort, the four-input model achieved 72.2% held-out classification accuracy, compared with 67.8% for a scalar-score model. A separate paired counterfactual experiment involving 600 matched systems demonstrated that the modeled closed-loop stabilizer increased simulated recovery from 45.2% to 68.8%, while reducing deterioration from 45.8% to 30.0%. The study also explores physics-informed neural network (PINN) trajectory reconstruction as a computational approach for estimating continuous cellular-state dynamics from sparse observations. A supplementary experiment examines a candidate recoverability function under two synthetic initial-condition scenarios. Collectively, these investigations provide an initial computational examination of cellular recoverability as a multidimensional, dynamic state-space problem. All reported results are based on synthetic data and specified modeling assumptions; experimental biological calibration, independent computational benchmarking, and further mathematical development remain necessary to establish biological validity.

papers.title: Applied solution techniques for bi-level problems in hydropower equivalent estimation
papers.abstract: Abstract Hydropower is able to provide flexibility for the energy system by saving water in a reservoir and, in some stations, also the possibility of pumping. However, modeling hydroelectric systems can be challenging due to the complexity of cascade river systems and data limitations. Energy system models are therefore often using a simplified approach called a "hydropower equivalent." Calculating an equivalent involves bi-level optimization that minimizes the differences between a detailed reference model and the simplified system. Previous research has demonstrated the flexibility and effectiveness of applying Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to solve bi-level optimization problems. However, its performance has not been compared to other search algorithms, such as Bayesian optimization and random sampling. This study examines the robustness of PSO solutions by comparing them with those of other methods. The Optuna framework is used in this research because it offers implementations of both random sampling and Bayesian optimization. Additionally, it provides a functional ANOVA (Analysis of Variance) to calculate the importance of individual variables, which enhances understanding of the solutions and highlights the significance of each variable. Furthermore, a new combined approach of Bayesian optimization and PSO is proposed. While PSO tends to be more accurate for complex equivalent systems with many parameters, Optuna’s framework provides significant advantages in parameter analysis. A combined approach employing both methods showed promising results for optimizing more complex models. Overall, Optuna enhances the understanding of each parameter’s impact, offering valuable insights for designing equivalent hydropower systems.

papers.abstract: This paper examines how interactive teaching methods can improve the quality of chemistry instruction in general secondary schools and universities. Chemistry is widely regarded as a difficult subject because students must connect observable phenomena with invisible particle-level processes and with symbolic notation. Traditional lecture-based teaching often leaves these connections to the learner and produces formal, memorised knowledge. Drawing on research on active learning, social constructivism and Johnstone's chemistry triangle, the paper analyses a set of interactive methods suited to chemistry: Think–Pair–Share, the Jigsaw technique, Peer Instruction with concept questions, Predict–Observe–Explain demonstrations, case studies, cluster and concept mapping, Process Oriented Guided Inquiry Learning (POGIL), role play and educational games, and digital simulations. For each method a concrete classroom example from the school chemistry curriculum is given. A model lesson structure that combines several methods and a set of practical recommendations for teachers are proposed. The paper concludes that interactive methods are most effective when they are chosen according to the learning objective, linked across the macroscopic, sub-microscopic and symbolic levels, and supported by formative assessment.

Responses were analyzed through frequency counts and mean scores to describe participants’ perceptions and reported practices. Findings indicated that most respondents regularly incorporated active learning strategies into their teaching and expressed favorable attitudes toward their implementation. Teachers perceived these approaches as encouraging student participation, strengthening the integration of learning, promoting classroom engagement, and supporting improvements in instructional practice. However, respondents also identified practical challenges that constrained implementation, including limited training and experience with active learning methodologies, inadequate funding for instructional materials, and classroom seating arrangements that were not conducive to interactive activities. The study recommends targeted professional development to strengthen teachers’ competence in active learning, revisions to departmental plans to facilitate the integration of these strategies, and improved consideration of classroom resources and learning environments. Further investigation from students’ perspectives is recommended to provide additional insight into how active learning is experienced and how it may contribute to learning outcomes in international school settings across the United Arab Emirates.

papers.title: Exigence and the Cognitive Kernel
papers.abstract: Computational systems routinely model tasks, priorities, deadlines, permissions, attention, and action, but they rarely possess a unified account of why a particular state presently calls for transition. This paper introduces Exigence as a first-class computational primitive: the graph-derived condition by which an object, process, agent, institution, or environment presently calls for some admissible change. Exigence is neither priority nor urgency. Priority is declared ordering; urgency concerns time sensitivity; Exigence arises from the live relationship between state, dependency, consequence, opportunity, authority, capability, care, safety, and constraint. The paper situates Exigence within a broader Cognitive Kernel, or CogK, that separates observation, salience, epistemic interpretation, Exigence, standing, attention, custody, sufficiency, policy, authorization, execution, receipt, and outcome. These elements are treated not as interchangeable stages but as distinct projections over shared governed reality. The separation allows systems to distinguish what is observed from what is believed, what matters from what may be done, and what may be done from what actually occurred. The resulting architecture supports lawful refusal, receipt-before-effect, context compilation, agent orchestration, institutional modeling, attention governance, household coordination, autonomous systems, games, simulated societies, and the progressive crystallization of expensive semantic reasoning into deterministic machinery. It also permits the modeling of pathological Exigence topologies such as fixation, suppression, inflation, avoidance, fragmentation, and over-propagation. These structures need not be used to diagnose humans. They can instead serve as integrity and execution-gate models for detecting recurrent computational trajectories that should be refused, escalated, reinterpreted, or repaired. The central claim is that Exigence is a candidate connective layer between a passive world model and governed transition. Its value depends on keeping an Exigence claim distinct from observation, salience, standing, attention, policy, authorization, effect, and outcome. The Cognitive Kernel thereby offers a general substrate for systems that must decide what currently matters, who holds the next move, what conditions are sufficient, what transitions are lawful, and when action must stop.

papers.title: Student Needs Analysis for Designing an Ethnobotany Based Ethno-Experiential Learning Model in Human Anatomy
papers.abstract: This study aimed to analyze student needs as an empirical basis for designing an ethnobotany-based Ethno-Experiential Learning Model for Human Anatomy education. This preliminary study employed a descriptive quantitative approach supported by qualitative data. Participants were 58 students who had completed a Human Anatomy course. Data were collected using a needs analysis questionnaire comprising 20 closed-ended statements rated on a four-point Likert scale and four open-ended questions. Descriptive statistics were used to analyze four aspects: Human Anatomy learning conditions, health literacy, science process skills (SPS), and needs for learning model development. The findings showed that 94.83% of students wanted more active learning involving direct experiences, while 96.55% reported that anatomical concepts were easier to understand when connected to everyday health issues. Regarding health literacy, 93.10% reported being able to access health information from reliable sources; however, 75.86% still experienced difficulties understanding such information. For SPS, collecting information or data received 87.93% agreement, whereas careful observation of health phenomena received the lowest agreement (70.69%). In addition, 98.28% of students supported connecting Human Anatomy with local medicinal plants and incorporating video or digital media, while 96.55% supported a model integrating health literacy and SPS. Responses to open-ended questions emphasized practical activities, visual representations, interactive media, group discussions, and real-world health contexts. These findings provide an empirical basis for designing an instructional framework that meaningfully connects local ethnobotanical knowledge, concrete experiences, scientific inquiry, digital resources, and anatomical concepts. Further research is needed to develop the model and evaluate its validity, practicality, and effectiveness.

papers.title: Case-based learning for facilities management education in a developing country context: bridging theory, practice and local realities
papers.abstract: Purpose Although case-based learning (CBL) has gained considerable attention as an active learning strategy in higher education, empirical evidence regarding its effectiveness in facilities management (FM) education, particularly within developing-country contexts, remains limited. This study examines the students' perceptions of CBL in relation to knowledge application, soft skills, learning preferences, and employability among FM undergraduates at a state university in Sri Lanka. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey generated 268 responses, of which 221 complete responses were retained for analysis. Descriptive statistics and Friedman tests were used to examine students' perceptions, learning preferences and differences across academic levels, with effect-size measures used to assess practical significance. Findings Students generally perceived CBL as contributing positively to knowledge application, critical thinking, self-directed learning, teamwork, engagement, and professional preparedness. They also associated CBL with greater confidence in problem-solving, decision-making under uncertainty, and handling industry-related responsibilities. Collaborative and application-oriented approaches, particularly group discussions and action-based activities, were preferred over more complex methods such as role-play and integrated project-based tasks. Overall, these findings are consistent with the principles of Experiential Learning Theory and Work-Integrated Learning, suggesting that CBL may provide a useful means of connecting academic learning with authentic professional contexts. Originality/value The study extends existing case-based learning research by providing discipline-specific empirical evidence from Facilities Management education in Sri Lanka, a developing-country context that remains underrepresented in the CBL literature. By examining students across multiple academic levels and comparing their perceptions of different CBL activities, the study provides context-sensitive insights for the design of practice-oriented FM curricula.

papers.title: Microstructure and mechanical response of LPBF-fabricated AZ91D magnesium alloy and TiB₂/AZ91D composite
papers.abstract: AZ91D magnesium alloy and 2 wt.% TiB₂/AZ91D composite were fabricated by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) to improve the stiffness of AZ-series magnesium alloys. The effects of LPBF processing parameters, TiB₂ addition and T4 heat treatment on defect characteristics, microstructure, Young’s modulus and tensile response were investigated. Under the best-performing LPBF condition within the investigated parameter range, the AZ91D alloy exhibited limited visible defects, fine equiaxed grains with an average size of approximately 3–4 µm, and discrete β-Mg₁₇Al₁₂ particles in the Mg matrix. The alloy fabricated under this condition achieved a yield strength of 219.1 ± 13.5 MPa, an ultimate tensile strength of 329.5 ± 0.4 MPa, and an elongation of 7.3 ± 1.4%. TiB₂ addition increased the Young’s modulus from 44.2 ± 1.2 GPa for AZ91D to 56.4 ± 1.0 GPa for the as-printed TiB₂/AZ91D composite, corresponding to an increase of approximately 28%. However, the as-printed composite showed reduced ultimate tensile strength and elongation compared with the AZ91D alloy fabricated under the best-performing condition, which can be associated with residual pores and local TiB₂-rich regions. After T4 treatment at 420 °C for 6 h followed by water quenching, the representative composite retained a high Young’s modulus of 56.2 ± 1.3 GPa. Although the yield strength decreased to 187.3 ± 2.1 MPa, the ultimate tensile strength and elongation increased to 317.3 ± 3.8 MPa and 6.7 ± 1.3%, respectively. The improved tensile deformation capability is likely related to the partial dissolution of β-Mg₁₇Al₁₂ during solution treatment. These results indicate that TiB₂ reinforcement combined with T4 treatment is an effective strategy for improving the stiffness of LPBF-fabricated AZ91D alloy while maintaining acceptable tensile ductility.

papers.title: Bayesian optimization-guided closed-loop morphology optimization of block copolymer blends via synchrotron X-ray scattering
papers.abstract: The utility of block copolymers (BCPs) in next-generation nanofabrication and optoelectronics is strictly governed by the long-range ordering and precise periodicity of their microphase-separated domains. However, navigating their multi-dimensional processing space to maximize this structural fidelity can be difficult. Conventional optimization relies on Edisonian trial-and-error, which is resource-intensive, slow, and often fails to identify the global optimum. Here, we address this challenge using a closed-loop morphology-optimization workflow that integrates synchrotron grazing-incidence small-angle X-ray scattering (GISAXS), automated scattering data analysis, and Gaussian process-driven Bayesian optimization (GP-BO). Applied to the swelling-induced assembly of poly(styrene-b-2-vinylpyridine) (S2VP) blends, the BO-guided closed-loop workflow explores the two-dimensional processing space defined by polymer blending ratio and solvent uptake. By jointly optimizing domain spacing and peak sharpness as a measure of structural ordering, the workflow identified target-satisfying conditions using approximately 30 experiments, more than two orders of magnitude fewer than required for uniform coverage at the stated resolution. Overall, we developed a constraint-aware acquisition strategy tailored to morphology optimization, in which domain spacing is treated as a feasibility constraint while structural ordering is optimized within the feasible region. This task-specific formulation differs from applying a standard GP-BO workflow and enables efficient navigation of a coupled landscape containing both monotonic and highly nonlinear responses.

papers.title: Integrating Project-Based Learning, Growth Mindset, and Cultural Literacy: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric Analysis in Ethnoscience Education
papers.abstract: Project based learning (PjBL) is widely used to promote active learning, yet its relationship with students’ growth mindset, particularly in ethnoscience and cultural literacy contexts, requires further examination. This study aimed to analyze the role of PjBL in supporting students’ growth mindset, identify emerging research trends, and examine research gaps related to ethnoscience and cultural literacy. A systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted following the preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA 2020) guidelines. Literature searches were performed using Scopus, Google Scholar, and ERIC, focusing on publications from 2020 to 2025. Twelve articles met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed using systematic mapping and narrative synthesis, complemented by bibliometric visualization with VOSviewer. The findings suggest that PjBL is associated with learning motivation, persistence, self-regulated learning, reflective thinking, collaboration, and critical thinking. The reviewed literature also indicates that ethnoscience can connect scientific concepts with local knowledge, while cultural literacy can support cultural awareness and contextual learning. However, studies explicitly integrating PjBL, growth mindset, ethnoscience, and cultural literacy remain limited. The bibliometric analysis further indicates connections between PjBL, growth mindset, critical thinking, collaborative learning, and sustainable education. These findings highlight the potential of culturally contextualized PjBL while emphasizing the need for stronger empirical evidence. Future research should examine these integrated approaches through rigorous experimental and mixed-method designs across diverse cultural and educational settings

papers.title: Sweet Success: Using Candy Land to Explore Gamification in Medical Education
papers.abstract: Audience: This session is intended for learners and educators interested in medical education, including medical students, residents, fellows, and faculty. Introduction/Background: Gamification is increasingly recognized as an effective strategy to enhance engagement, motivation, and active learning in medical education. Despite its potential, many educators are unsure how to implement gamified strategies effectively. This session demonstrates a practical, interactive approach to applying gamification principles in a collaborative educational setting. Educational Objectives: By the end of this session, learners will be able to (1) describe key principles of gamification in medical education, (2) identify resources and tools for implementing gamification, (3) actively participate in a gamified educational activity, and (4) design a simple plan to implement gamification in their own teaching, considering benefits and potential challenges. Educational Methods: The session started with brief didactic lecture on game-based learning and gamification intended to orient participants to the material. Participants then engaged in a Candy Land-inspired, team-based activity. Twenty-five prompts covering aspects of gamification were arranged along a winding pathway drawn with chalk. Teams of 3–4 learners advanced along the path by rolling a large inflatable die and answering questions or discussing scenarios associated with the prompts. Correct answers earned points or allowed teams to advance, while debriefing discussions linked gameplay to the principles and strategies of gamification. Incorrect answers were not penalized. This approach leveraged experiential learning, active learning, and social constructivist principles to support both knowledge acquisition and practical application. Research Methods: The session was evaluated through direct observation and informal feedback from learners and instructors. Engagement, discussion quality, and participation were used as primary indicators of effectiveness. Modifications and recommendations for future implementation were derived from observed challenges and learner feedback. Results: Fifteen learners of varied training levels participated. Observations indicated high engagement, lively discussion, and collaborative problem-solving. Feedback was universally positive, with learners reporting increased confidence in understanding gamification principles and motivation to apply these strategies in their own teaching. Several participants subsequently incorporated gamified activities into educational sessions in the following weeks. Key lessons for implementation included ensuring sufficient space, clarifying scoring systems, and preparing materials in advance. Discussion: This session demonstrates that gamification can effectively engage learners across multiple levels, promote collaborative learning, and provide practical insights into implementation strategies. Learners experienced the mechanics and benefits of gamification firsthand, while also reflecting on challenges and planning for real-world application. The activity highlights how structured games can create a safe and inclusive learning environment, fostering participation from all learners. Future iterations may further optimize space, scoring, and team organization to enhance learning outcomes.

papers.title: DEAba: A Paper-Based, Data-Driven Methodology for Deep Learning of Metabolism
papers.abstract: Abstract Mastering metabolic concepts remains a persistent challenge for undergraduate students due to the abstract nature of the concepts, the intricate pathway interconnections, and the necessity of integrative reasoning. The common focus of prior educational stages on low-order cognitive assessment exacerbates this challenge, reinforcing surface-level learning and leading to widespread underpreparedness in incoming students. To address this systemic issue, we developed the Differential Expression Analysis-based activity (DEAba): a cooperative, paper-based yet data-intensive methodology that engages students in interpreting adapted real-world omics data sets. Grounded in established learning frameworks (Cognitive Load Theory, ICAP, and Bloom’s taxonomy), DEAba combines data-driven reasoning with analog collaboration to foster conceptual integration and address the high intrinsic cognitive load of metabolism. Across seven academic years (n = 1,212 students) in an undergraduate Biochemistry course, DEAba implementation was associated with significant improvements in final exam performance (p = 0.001), exam participation, and pass rates, while perception surveys revealed high levels of perceived usefulness, engagement, and conceptual clarity. These findings suggest that theoretically grounded, low-cost analog designs may support improved learning outcomes in challenging biochemical topics. DEAba offers instructors a scalable, evidence-based, and readily transferable tool for promoting active learning and deep, integrated understanding of metabolism without requiring technological infrastructure.

papers.abstract: Abstract Dams are important structures whose seismic safety needs to be assessed. During an earthquake, the dam body experience inertia forces while the reservoir water produces additional hydrodynamic pressure, with the response also being influenced by dam-reservoir and foundation interactions. This review synthesizes the research presented in the supplied literature on seismic behaviour of concrete gravity and earth dams. The reviewed studies employ seismic-coefficient procedures, response-spectrum and time-history methods, finite-element analysis, nonlinear soil models and Newmark-type deformation analysis. Particular attention is given to soil properties, dam geometry, foundation conditions, water pressure, soil plasticity and liquefaction. The literature indicates that simplified approaches areuseful for preliminary assessment, whereas dynamic and nonlinear numerical methods provide more accurate information about stresses, displacements and potential damage. Three-dimensional modelling can provide improved representation when adequate site and material data are available. Liquefaction is identified as a major hazard for susceptible sandy and gravelly foundation soils, and ground-improvement measures such as vibratory compaction and jet grouting have been investigated. Future research should emphasize nonlinear dam–reservoir–foundation interaction, uncertainty quantification, probabilistic assessment and integration of monitoring data with numerical models.

papers.title: Chance-Constrained Stochastic MPC to Deterministic Second-Order Cone Programming Equivalents for Lossy Satellite Links.
papers.abstract: Abstract— Unmanned aerial vehicle navigation under lossy satellite backhauls demands robust probabilistic safety guarantees. This paper reformulates joint chance-constraints into deterministic Second-Order Cone Programming (SOCP) equivalents, ensuring rigorous constraint satisfaction under packet jitter, Age-of-Information (AoI) degradation, and telemetry latency. By integrating satellite-terrestrial telemetry via NigComSat-1R parameters, the proposed receding horizon Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework guarantees recursive feasibility and robust collision avoidance within 4D Cylindrical Volume Exclusion (CVE) models. Comprehensive MATLAB numerical simulations validate that the derived SOCP formulation maintains strict spatial safety margins under severe packet dropout rates while satisfying real-time onboard solver execution limits.

papers.title: Yoga as an Indian Knowledge System for Holistic Education: A Critical Review of Physical Health, Mental Well-Being, and Learning Outcomes
papers.abstract: Holistic education seeks to support learners’ physical, cognitive, emotional, social, ethical, and reflective development rather than treating academic attainment as its sole purpose. Yoga, understood as a diverse Indian knowledge tradition and not merely a collection of postures, offers one possible framework for connecting these dimensions. This critical review examines the philosophical and educational foundations of yoga and evaluates contemporary research concerning physical health, mental well-being, attention, self-regulation, and learning-related outcomes. A narrative, critical approach was used to bring together classical yoga literature, education policy documents, public-health guidance, systematic reviews, and selected intervention studies relevant to school and higher-education settings. The literature suggests that appropriately adapted yoga programmes may contribute to flexibility, balance, body awareness, stress management, emotional regulation, and some aspects of attention and psychological well-being. Nevertheless, the evidence is heterogeneous: programmes differ in content, duration, instructor preparation, comparison conditions, outcome measures, and methodological quality. Evidence that yoga independently improves grades or broad academic achievement is less conclusive than evidence for selected psychosocial outcomes. The article argues that yoga can support holistic education when it is taught inclusively, safely, developmentally, and in a culturally informed manner; when it complements rather than replaces physical education, counselling, medical care, and active learning; and when its effects are evaluated transparently. Practical recommendations are proposed for curriculum design, teacher preparation, safeguarding, assessment, and future research. The central conclusion is that yoga’s educational value lies not in promises of universal transformation, but in the careful integration of embodied practice, attention, reflection, ethical inquiry, and evidence-informed pedagogy. Keywords: learning outcomes; Indian Knowledge Systems; Yoga; Mental Well-being; holistic education; physical health; school education; evidence-informed pedagogy

papers.title: Effect of Intraoperative Subanesthetic-Dose Esketamine on Postoperative Hydromorphone Consumption After Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Randomized Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Trial
papers.abstract: Background: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated whether intraoperative subanesthetic-dose esketamine reduces postoperative opioid consumption and improves early recovery outcomes after total hip arthroplasty (THA). Methods: A total of 128 patients was randomized to receive esketamine (Group E, n = 64) or saline (Group C, n = 64). Group E received an intravenous esketamine bolus of 0.25 mg/kg 5 minutes before skin incision, followed by a 0.25 mg/kg/h infusion until skin closure. Group C received an equivalent volume of normal saline using the same regimen. Postoperative analgesia was provided by patient-controlled intravenous analgesia with hydromorphone. The primary outcome was the cumulative hydromorphone consumption during the first 24 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes included 48-h hydromorphone consumption, Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) pain scores, quality of recovery (QoR-15), Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS), mood, and adverse events. Postoperative sleep disturbance (PSD) was assessed as an exploratory outcome. Results: The first 24-h hydromorphone consumption was significantly lower in Group E than in Group C (2.24 [2.08– 2.51] vs 3.20 [2.88– 3.40] mg, P < 0.001). Cumulative hydromorphone consumption over the first 48 h was also lower in Group E (4.40 [4.16– 4.82] vs 5.92 [5.30– 6.23] mg, P < 0.001). Group E had lower NRS scores at 6 and 24 h. On postoperative day 1, Group E exhibited higher QoR-15 scores and lower AIS scores ( P < 0.05), and the incidence of PSD was significantly lower in Group E than in Group C (26.6% vs 54.7%, P = 0.001). Adverse event rates did not differ significantly between groups ( P > 0.05). Conclusion: Intraoperative subanesthetic-dose esketamine reduced the first 24-h hydromorphone consumption after THA. Findings for the secondary outcomes are exploratory and require confirmation in future studies. Trial Registration: ChiCTR2600116506. Keywords: esketamine, total hip arthroplasty, opioid consumption, postoperative recovery, sleep quality

papers.title: Neuronal World: Illusionistic Explanation of the Empirical Reality
papers.abstract: The neurophilosophical concept of the neuronal world posits that brain rhythms create a three-dimensional holographic virtual reality. The neuronal world model argues that virtual reality is a continuous construct of the brain, crafted through the electromagnetic synchronisation of neurons. Brain activity generates the empirical world through a dynamic interaction of sensory inputs and resonant neuronal states. The neuronal world comprises two basic models — the world model and the self-model — each composed of many levels. Basic neuronal rhythms, such as gamma and alpha oscillations, realise sensory integration and abstract dissociation. High-frequency gamma rhythms construct the empirical world and create detailed sensory experiences, while alpha and beta rhythms decompose sensory data into more abstract layers. Neuronal activity results in a coherent, integrated simulation. A clearer account of the true nature of reality is therefore important for the formation of a detailed and consistent neurophilosophical worldview. Understanding how brain activity constructs the experience of reality is critical not only for theoretical explanation but also for explaining various brain disorders that lead to psychiatric disturbance. In this context, the article examines major depressive disorder as a possible disturbance of the rhythmic mechanisms underlying the neuronal world, challenges the conventional neurotransmitter-based account of depression, and develops the concept of neuro-illusionistic therapy as a possible therapeutic framework. This article aims to describe how the brain simulates virtual reality from the perspective of the neuronal world model and to explain basic neurogenerative mechanisms that construct the neurosimulation

papers.title: Analysis of Thermo-Hydraulic Behavior of a Compact Heat Exchanger with TPMS Structures
papers.abstract: This paper presents the design and numerical evaluation of a compact heat exchanger employing TPMS (Triply Periodic Minimal Surfaces) structures. Attention is focused on the characteristics of selected TPMS structures, their implementation in the heat exchanger design, and the selection of a suitable geometric configuration in terms of thermal performance and pressure losses. The heat exchanger geometry was designed in Creo Parametric, while the TPMS structures themselves were generated using nTop software. Their thermo-hydraulic properties were evaluated by numerical simulations in ANSYS CFX, focusing on the influence of geometric and operating parameters. Based on the numerical simulation results, the most suitable variant was selected as a compromise between the achieved thermal performance and hydraulic losses.
